analysis.recent_context: Friday 31 July SGT produced a 105-message fire drill: Payntra, Syntra and Baymax-pipeline-probe all returned 502 from Caddy because host systemd Caddy was trying to DNS-resolve container hostnames. Fix was host-port mappings (127.0.0.1:32769, 8081, 8082) plus four Caddyfile rewrites; all four domains returned 200 within 12 minutes. Since then the system has been quiet across the weekend — daily email brief, morning brief, baymax backup, and bi-daily Hermes update all completed on schedule through 02 Aug 06:00 SGT. No new user contact since the incident.

recommendations.reason: The 31 Jul fire drill produced a clear, reusable rule: host Caddy + 127.0.0.1:HOSTPORT per project, never bare container hostnames. The entry is staged for /memory approval but not yet committed. Without it, the lesson lives only in session history and the next Baymax session starts blind to the pattern.
recommendations.action: Run /memory pending, review the entry, and approve it. Takes 30 seconds; prevents the next 502 regression. Do this first thing — before Monday traffic ramps.

recommendations.title: Schedule the Caddy-to-container consolidation for a low-traffic window
recommendations.reason: The current state works but is fragile: a dead docker-proxy on any project reproduces the same 502 (proven Friday). The cleaner architecture is Caddy as a container on the shared `web` network, which is what the original /srv/caddy/docker-compose.yml was set up to do. Three projects, four Caddy sites, one compose file. ~1–2 hours of work.
recommendations.action: Pick a quiet window (Sunday afternoon or Monday evening) and convert: bring Caddy up as a container attached to `web`, drop the 127.0.0.1:PORT mappings from payntra/syntra/baymax-pipeline-probe docker-compose files, restore the original reverse_proxy host:port lines in Caddyfile sites, reload. Verify each domain returns 200.
